content: Pirbuterol is a beta-2 adrenergic agonist that is approved by the FDA for the treatment of bronchospasm in patients aged 12 years and older who have reversible bronchospasm, including asthma. It is commonly associated with side effects such as nervousness and tremor. The MAXAIR inhaler is specifically indicated for the prevention and reversal of bronchospasm in patients aged 12 years and older. It can be used either alone or in combination with theophylline and/or corticosteroid therapy. The standard dosage for adults and children aged 12 years and older is two inhalations (400 mcg) every 4 to 6 hours. In some cases, one inhalation (200 mcg) every 4 to 6 hours may suffice. The total daily dose should not exceed 12 inhalations. If the usual dosage fails to provide relief, this may indicate a significant worsening of asthma, and immediate medical attention is required. Before using the MAXAIR inhaler for the first time, or if it has not been used for more than two weeks, it should be primed by releasing three test sprays into the air, away from yourself and others. The MAXAIR inhaler is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to pirbuterol or any of its components. These effects are uncommon at recommended doses but may necessitate discontinuation of the drug. Patients with cardiovascular disorders, such as coronary insufficiency, arrhythmias, or hypertension, should use the inhaler with caution. Additionally, the inhaler may cause paradoxical bronchospasm, which can be life-threatening. If this occurs, the inhaler should be discontinued immediately, and alternative therapy should be initiated. Beta-agonist bronchodilators, including pirbuterol, may not be sufficient to control asthma in many patients. Early consideration should be given to adding anti-inflammatory agents, such as corticosteroids. If a patient requires more frequent doses of the inhaler than usual, this may indicate worsening asthma, necessitating a reassessment of the treatment plan. Pirbuterol should be used cautiously in patients with cardiovascular disorders, hyperthyroidism, diabetes mellitus, or those who are unusually sensitive to sympathomimetic amines. It may cause transient hypokalemia, which could lead to adverse cardiovascular effects. Adverse reactions reported in clinical trials include nervousness (6.9%), tremor (6.0%), headache (2.0%), dizziness (1.2%), palpitations (1.7%), tachycardia (1.2%), cough (1.2%), and nausea (1.7%). Less common adverse effects include depression, anxiety, confusion, insomnia, weakness, syncope, hypotension, chest pain, dry mouth, abdominal pain, rash, and fatigue. Rarely, ECG changes and arrhythmias have been observed. Pirbuterol should not be used concurrently with other short-acting beta-adrenergic bronchodilators due to the risk of additive effects. It should also be used cautiously in patients taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors or tricyclic antidepressants, as these drugs may potentiate its effects on the vascular system. Beta-blockers may antagonize the effects of pirbuterol and can cause severe bronchospasm in asthmatic patients. If beta-blockers are necessary, cardioselective agents should be used with caution. Co-administration with non-potassium-sparing diuretics may exacerbate hypokalemia and ECG changes. Pirbuterol is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA. Animal studies have not shown teratogenic effects at doses up to 1000 times the maximum recommended daily inhalation dose for humans. However, at very high doses, fetal death and abortions were observed in animal studies. There are no adequate studies in pregnant women, so pirbuterol should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefits outweigh the risks. Its safety during labor and delivery is not well established, and it should be used with caution due to its potential to interfere with uterine contractility. It is unknown whether pirbuterol is excreted in human milk, so caution is advised when administering it to nursing mothers. The MAXAIR inhaler is not recommended for use in children under 12 years of age due to insufficient safety and efficacy data. There is no specific guidance on its use in geriatric patients, individuals with renal or hepatic impairment, or specific gender or racial populations. The pharmacologic effects of pirbuterol are mediated through stimulation of beta-2 adrenergic receptors, leading to increased intracellular cyclic AMP levels. This results in relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle and inhibition of the release of hypersensitivity mediators from mast cells. Pirbuterol has a preferential effect on beta-2 adrenergic receptors compared to beta-1 receptors, although beta-2 receptors are also present in the human heart. The MAXAIR inhaler contains pirbuterol acetate, a white crystalline powder that is freely soluble in water. Each actuation delivers 200 mcg of pirbuterol from the mouthpiece. The inhaler should be stored at temperatures between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F) and kept away from heat or open flames. The canister should not be punctured or exposed to temperatures above 120°F. It should be discarded after 300 actuations, even if it is not completely empty. Patients should be counseled on the proper use of the MAXAIR inhaler, including priming, cleaning, and tracking the number of actuations. They should not exceed the recommended dose or frequency and should seek medical attention if their symptoms worsen or if the inhaler becomes less effective. Common side effects include palpitations, chest pain, rapid heart rate, tremor, and nervousness.
